# f5xc_route (Data Source)

route object is used to configuring L7 routing decision. route is made of three things<br>1. Match condition for incoming request<br>2. Actions to take if match is true<br>3. Whether custom java script processing is enabled for this route match.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Route - Full

data "f5xc_route" "example" {
  name      = f5xc_route.example.name
  namespace = f5xc_route.example.namespace
}
```

### Optional

- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

Headers specified at this level are applied before headers from the enclosing VirtualHost object level (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add))
- `response_headers_to_remove` (List of String) Header to be removed from response List of keys of Headers to be removed from the HTTP response being sent towards downstream.
- `route_action_choice` (Attributes) route_action one of action to take when match is successful (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice))

- `waf_exclusion_choice` (Attributes) Enable the WAF Exclusion functionality for VirtualHost WAF Exclusion details at the route level The WAF Exclusion is evaluated sequentially and can only be matched once per request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--waf_exclusion_choice))
- `waf_type` (Attributes) Enable the WAF (Web Application Firewall) functionality for Route WAF can be used to analyze inbound and outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic. WAF can be configured either in BLOCKing Mode or ALERTing Mode. In BLOCKing mode if WAF detects suspicious inbound/outbound traffic it blocks the request or response. In ALERTing mode if suspicious traffic is detected, WAF generates ALERTs with details on the suspicious traffic (instead of blocking traffic). waf_type is the App Firewall profile to use. waf_type specified at route level overrides waf configuration at VirtualHost level (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--waf_type))

- `append` (Boolean) append Should the value be appended? If true, the value is appended to existing values. Default value is do not append
- `name` (String) name Name of the HTTP header.
- `value_choice` (Attributes) value Enter Header value as string or blindfolded secret. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response_headers_to_add.value_choice`

Read-Only:

- `secret_value` (Attributes) Secret Value Secret Value of the HTTP header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value))
- `value` (String) value Value of the HTTP header.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response_headers_to_add.value_choice.secret_value`

Read-Only:

- `secret_info_choice` (Attributes) SecretInfoOneof Secret can be one of the following types - * Blindfold Secret - Secret is managed by F5XC Secret Management System * Clear Secret - Secret is not encrypted (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response_headers_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice`

Read-Only:

- `blindfold_secret_info` (Attributes) Blindfold Secret Blindfold Secret is used for the secrets managed by F5XC Secret Management Service (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info))
- `clear_secret_info` (Attributes) Clear Secret Clear Secret is used for the secrets that are not encrypted (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info))
- `none` (Boolean) None No private key will be stored or used. Choose this only when you need a public certificate for verification (e.g., validating SAML/JWT signatures). Not suitable for TLS or any use case that requires presenting a certificate, those will fail without a private key.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response_headers_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice.blindfold_secret_info`

Read-Only:

- `decryption_provider` (String) Decryption Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the backend Secret Management service.
- `location` (String) Location Location is the uri_ref. It could be in url format for string:/// Or it could be a path if the store provider is an http/https location
- `store_provider` (String) Store Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///


<a id="nestedatt--routes--response_headers_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response_headers_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice.clear_secret_info`

Read-Only:

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///
- `url` (String, Sensitive) URL URL of the secret. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, Secret needs to be encoded Base64 format. When asked for this secret, caller will get Secret bytes after Base64 decoding.






<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice`

Read-Only:

- `route_destination` (Attributes) route_destination Send request to one of the destination from list of destinations (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination))
- `route_direct_response` (Attributes) route_direct_response Send direct response (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_direct_response))
- `route_redirect` (Attributes) route_redirect Send redirect response (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination`

Read-Only:

- `buffer_policy` (Attributes) buffer_policy Buffering configuration for requests Some upstream applications are not capable of handling streamed data. This config enables buffering the entire request before sending to upstream application. We can specify the maximum buffer size and buffer interval with this config. Route level buffer configuration overrides any configuration at VirtualHost level. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--buffer_policy))
- `cluster_retract_choice` (Attributes) Oneof for Cluster retraction Specifies whether retraction of cluster has to be enabled or disabled (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--cluster_retract_choice))
- `cors_policy` (Attributes) cors_policy Cross-Origin Resource Sharing requests configuration CORS is a mechanism that uses additional HTTP headers to tell a browser to let a web application running at one origin (domain) have permission to access selected resources from a server at a different origin (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--cors_policy))
- `csrf_policy` (Attributes) csrf_policy Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that occurs when a malicious third-party website exploits a vulnerability thats allows them to submit an undesired request on user's behalf. The policy checks where a request is coming from to determine if the request's origin is the same as its destination. The policy relies on two pieces of information used in determining if a request originated from the same host. 1. The origin that caused the user agent to issue the request (source origin). 2. The origin that the request is going to (target origin). When the policy evaluating a request, it ensures both pieces of information are present and compare their values. If the source origin is missing or origins do not match the request is rejected. The exception to this being the source-origin has been added to the policy as valid. Because CSRF attacks specifically target state-changing requests, the policy only acts on the HTTP requests that have state-changing method (PUT,POST, etc.). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy))
- `destinations` (Attributes List) destinations When requests have to distributed among multiple upstream clusters, multiple destinations are configured, each having its own cluster and weight. Traffic is distributed among clusters based on the weight configured. Example: destinations: - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-1 weight: 20 - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-2 weight: 30 - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-3 weight: 50 This indicates that out of every 100 requests, 50 goes to cluster-3, 30 to cluster-2 and 20 to cluster-1 When single destination is configured, weight is ignored. All the requests are sent to the cluster specified in the destination (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--destinations))
- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) endpoint_subsets Upstream cluster may be configured to divide its endpoints into subsets based on metadata attached to the endpoints. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer Labels field of endpoint object's metadata is used for subset matching. For endpoint's which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those endpoints of upstream cluster which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `hash_policy` (Attributes List) hash_policy Specifies a list of hash policies to use for ring hash load balancing. Each hash policy is evaluated individually and the combined result is used to route the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy))
- `host_rewrite_params_choice` (Attributes) HostRewriteParams Specifies how the host header can be modified during forwarding (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--host_rewrite_params_choice))
- `mirror_policy` (Attributes) mirror_policy MirrorPolicy is used for shadowing traffic from one cluster to another. The current implementation is 'fire and forget,' meaning it will not wait for the shadow cluster to respond before returning the response from the primary cluster. All normal statistics are collected for the shadow cluster making this feature useful for testing. During shadowing, the host/authority header is altered such that *-shadow* is appended. This is useful for logging. For example, *cluster1* becomes *cluster1-shadow*. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--mirror_policy))
- `priority` (List of String) priority Priority routing for each route. Different connection pools are used based on the priority of the route. Also, circuit-breaker configuration at destination cluster is chosen based on the route priority.
- `query_params` (Attributes) query_params Handling of incoming query parameters in simple route. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--query_params))
- `retry_policy` (Attributes) retry_policy Indicates that the route has a retry policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--retry_policy))
- `route_destination_rewrite_choice` (Attributes) RouteDestinationRewrite Specifies how the path can be modified during forwarding (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--route_destination_rewrite_choice))
- `spdy_config` (Attributes) spdy_config SPDY configuration for each route (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--spdy_config))
- `timeout` (Number) timeout Specifies the timeout for the route in milliseconds. This timeout includes all retries. For server side streaming, configure this field with higher value or leave it un-configured for infinite timeout
- `web_socket_config` (Attributes) web_socket_config Websocket configuration for each route (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--web_socket_config))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--buffer_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.buffer_policy`

Read-Only:

- `disabled` (Boolean) disable Disable buffering for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has buffering, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host
- `max_request_bytes` (Number) max_request_bytes The maximum request size that the filter will buffer before the connection manager will stop buffering and return a RequestEntityTooLarge (413) response.


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--cluster_retract_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.cluster_retract_choice`

Read-Only:

- `do_not_retract_cluster` (Boolean) do_not_retract_cluster When this option is configured, cluster with no healthy endpoints is not retracted from route having weighted cluster configuration.
- `retract_cluster` (Boolean) retract_cluster When this option is enabled, weighted cluster will not be considered for loadbalancing, if all its endpoints are unhealthy. Since the cluster with all unhealthy endpoints is removed, the traffic will be distributed among remaining clusters as per their weight. Also panic-threshold configuration is ignored for retracted cluster. This option is ignored when single destination cluster is configured for route


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--cors_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.cors_policy`

Read-Only:

- `allow_credentials` (Boolean) allow_credentials Specifies whether the resource allows credentials
- `allow_headers` (String) allow_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-headers header
- `allow_methods` (String) allow_methods Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-methods header
- `allow_origin` (List of String) allow_origin Specifies the origins that will be allowed to do CORS requests. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `allow_origin_regex` (List of String) allow_origin_regex Specifies regex patterns that match allowed origins. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `disabled` (Boolean) disabled Disable the CorsPolicy for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has CorsPolicy, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host
- `expose_headers` (String) expose_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-expose-headers header
- `maximum_age` (Number) maximum_age This indicates the maximum number of seconds the results can be cached A value of -1 will disable caching. Maximum permitted value is 86400 seconds (24 hours)


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.csrf_policy`

Read-Only:

- `allowed_domains_choice` (Attributes) allowed_domains The list of source origin that should be allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.csrf_policy.allowed_domains_choice`

Read-Only:

- `all_load_balancer_domains` (Boolean) all_load_balancer_domains Add All load balancer domains to source origin (allow) list.
- `custom_domain_list` (Attributes) custom_domain_list Add one or more domains to source origin (allow) list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice--custom_domain_list))
- `disabled` (Boolean) disabled Allow all source origin domains.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice--custom_domain_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.csrf_policy.allowed_domains_choice.custom_domain_list`

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domain names that will be matched to loadbalancer. These domains are not used for SNI match. Wildcard names are supported in the suffix or prefix form.




<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--destinations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.destinations`

Read-Only:

- `cluster` (Attributes List) cluster Indicates the upstream cluster to which the request should be sent. If the cluster does not exist ServiceUnavailable response will be sent (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--destinations--cluster))
- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) endpoint_subsets Upstream cluster may be configured to divide its endpoints into subsets based on metadata attached to the endpoints. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer Labels field of endpoint object's metadata is used for subset matching. For endpoints which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those endpoints of upstream cluster which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `priority` (Number) Priority Priority of this cluster, valid only with multiple destinations are configured. Value of 0 will make the cluster as lowest priority upstream cluster Priority of 1 means highest priority and is considered active. When active cluster is not available, lower priority clusters are made active as per the increasing priority.
- `weight` (Number) weight When requests have to distributed among multiple upstream clusters, multiple destinations are configured, each having its own cluster and weight. Traffic is distributed among clusters based on the weight configured. Example: destinations: - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-1 weight: 20 - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-2 weight: 30 - cluster: - kind: ves.io.vega.cfg.adc.cluster.Object uid: cluster-3 weight: 10 This indicates that out of every 60 requests, 10 goes to cluster-3, 30 to cluster-2 and 20 to cluster-1 When single destination is configured, weight is ignored. All the requests are sent to the cluster specified in the destination

- `terminal` (Boolean) terminal Specify if its a terminal policy

- `header_name` (String) Header The name or key of the request header that will be used to obtain the hash key
- `source_ip` (Boolean) Source IP Hash based on source IP address

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie`

Read-Only:

- `httponly_choice` (Attributes) httponly A cookie with the HttpOnly attribute is inaccessible to the JavaScript. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--httponly_choice))
- `name` (String) name The name of the cookie that will be used to obtain the hash key. If the cookie is not present and TTL below is not set, no hash will be produced
- `path` (String) path The name of the path for the cookie. If no path is specified here, no path will be set for the cookie
- `samesite_choice` (Attributes) samesite Controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice))
- `secure_choice` (Attributes) secure A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol and therefore, is more resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--secure_choice))
- `ttl` (Number) ttl If specified, a cookie with the TTL will be generated if the cookie is not present. If the TTL is present and zero, the generated cookie will be a session cookie. TTL value is in milliseconds

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--httponly_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.httponly_choice`

Read-Only:

- `ignore_httponly` (Boolean) ignore_httponly Ignore httponly attribute


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.samesite_choice`

Read-Only:

- `ignore_samesite` (Boolean) ignore_samesite Ignore Samesite attribute
- `samesite_lax` (Boolean) lax Add Samesite attribute with Lax. Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests
- `samesite_none` (Boolean) none Add Samesite attribute with None. Means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests
- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--retry_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.retry_policy`

Read-Only:

- `back_off` (Attributes) Retry BackOff Specifies parameters that control retry back off. This parameter is optional, in which case the default base interval is 25 milliseconds. The default maximum interval is 10 times the base interval (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--retry_policy--back_off))
- `num_retries` (Number) num_retries Specifies the allowed number of retries. Defaults to 1. Retries can be done any number of times. An exponential back-off algorithm is used between each retry
- `per_try_timeout` (Number) per_try_timeout Specifies a non-zero timeout per retry attempt. In milliseconds
- `retriable_status_codes` (List of Number) Retriable status Code HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry in addition to those specified by retry_on.
- `retry_condition` (List of String) retry_condition Specifies the conditions under which retry takes place. Retries can be on different types of condition depending on application requirements. For example, network failure, all 5xx response codes, idempotent 4xx response codes, etc The possible values are '5xx'             : Retry will be done if the upstream server responds with any 5xx response code, or does not respond at all (disconnect/reset/read timeout). 'gateway-error'   : Retry will be done only if the upstream server responds with 502, 503 or 504 responses (Included in 5xx) 'connect-failure' : Retry will be done if the request fails because of a connection failure to the upstream server (connect timeout, etc.). (Included in 5xx) 'refused-stream'  : Retry is done if the upstream server resets the stream with a REFUSED_STREAM error code (Included in 5xx) 'retriable-4xx'   : Retry is done if the upstream server responds with a retriable 4xx response code. The only response code in this category is HTTP CONFLICT (409) 'retriable-status-codes' :  Retry is done if the upstream server responds with any response code matching one defined in retriable_status_codes field 'reset'           : Retry is done if the upstream server does not respond at all (disconnect/reset/read timeout.)

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--retry_policy--back_off"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.retry_policy.back_off`

Read-Only:

- `base_interval` (Number) base_interval Specifies the base interval between retries in milliseconds
- `max_interval` (Number) max_interval Specifies the maximum interval between retries in milliseconds. This parameter is optional, but must be greater than or equal to the base_interval if set. The default is 10 times the base_interval.



<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--route_destination_rewrite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.route_destination_rewrite_choice`

Read-Only:

- `prefix_rewrite` (String) prefix_rewrite prefix_rewrite indicates that during forwarding, the matched prefix (or path) should be swapped with its value. When using regex path matching, the entire path (not including the query string) will be swapped with this value. This option allows application URLs to be rooted at a different path from those exposed at the reverse proxy layer. Example : gcSpec: routes: - match: - headers: [] path: prefix : /register/ query_params: [] - headers: [] path: prefix: /register query_params: [] routeDestination: prefixRewrite: '/' destinations: - cluster: - kind: cluster.Object uid: cluster-1 Having above entries in the config, requests to /register will be stripped to /, while requests to /register/public will be stripped to /public
- `regex_rewrite` (Attributes) regex_rewrite regex_rewrite indicates that during forwarding, the matched regex should be swapped with the substitution value. Example : gcSpec: routes: - match: - headers: [] path: regex : '^/service/([^/]+)(/.*)$' query_params: [] routeDestination: regexRewrite: pattern: '^/service/([^/]+)(/.*)$' substitution: '\\2/instance/\\1' destinations: - cluster: - kind: cluster.Object uid: cluster-1 The path pattern '^/service/([^/]+)(/.*)$' paired with a substitution string of '\\2/instance/\\1' would transform '/service/foo/v1/api' into '/v1/api/instance/foo'. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--route_destination_rewrite_choice--regex_rewrite))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--route_destination_rewrite_choice--regex_rewrite"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.route_destination_rewrite_choice.regex_rewrite`

Read-Only:

- `pattern` (String) Pattern The regular expression used to find portions of a string that should be replaced.
- `substitution` (String) Substitution The string that should be substituted into matching portions of the subject string during a substitution operation to produce a new string.



<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--spdy_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_destination.spdy_config`

Read-Only:

- `use_spdy` (Boolean) use_spdy Specifies that the HTTP client connection to this route is allowed to upgrade to a SPDY connection


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_destination--web_socket_config"></a>

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_direct_response"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_direct_response`

Read-Only:

- `response_body_encoded` (String) response_body Response body to send. Currently supported URL schemes is string:/// for which message should be encoded in Base64 format. The message can be either plain text or html. E.g. '<p> Access Denied </p>'. Base64 encoded string url for this is string:///PHA+IEFjY2VzcyBEZW5pZWQgPC9wPg==
- `response_code` (Number) response_code response code to send


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_redirect`

Read-Only:

- `host_redirect` (String) host_redirect swap host part of incoming URL in redirect URL
- `proto_redirect` (String) proto_redirect swap protocol part of incoming URL in redirect URL The protocol can be swapped with either http or https When incoming-proto option is specified, swapping of protocol is not done.
- `query_params_choice` (Attributes) query_params handling of incoming query parameters in redirect request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect--query_params_choice))
- `redirect_path_choice` (Attributes) Redirect Path Path in the redirect response (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect--redirect_path_choice))
- `response_code` (Number) response_code The HTTP status code to use in the redirect response.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect--query_params_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_redirect.query_params_choice`

Read-Only:

- `remove_all_params` (Boolean) Remove All Params
- `replace_params` (String) Replace All Params
- `retain_all_params` (Boolean) Retain All Params


<a id="nestedatt--routes--route_action_choice--route_redirect--redirect_path_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.route_action_choice.route_redirect.redirect_path_choice`

Read-Only:

- `path_redirect` (String) path_redirect swap path part of incoming URL in redirect URL
- `prefix_rewrite` (String) prefix_rewrite In Redirect response, the matched prefix (or path) should be swapped with this value. This option allows redirect URLs be dynamically created based on the request

<a id="nestedatt--routes--waf_type"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.waf_type`

Read-Only:

- `ref_type_choice` (Attributes) Web Application Firewall (WAF) WAF can be used to analyze inbound and outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic. WAF can be configured either in BLOCKing Mode or ALERTing Mode. In BLOCKing mode if WAF detects suspicious inbound/outbound traffic it blocks the request or response. In ALERTing mode if suspicious traffic is detected, WAF generates ALERTs with details on the suspicious traffic (instead of blocking traffic). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--waf_type--ref_type_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--waf_type--ref_type_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.waf_type.ref_type_choice`

- `disable_waf` (Boolean) disable app firewall No App Firewall enforcement
- `inherit_waf` (Boolean) inherit app firewall Any App Firewall configuration that was configured on a higher level will be enforced
